name: Ocean Green
lede: Ocean Green is a clear, medium sea-green, and one of the few color names whose dictionary definition does not match its own standard swatch.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson defines ocean green as a yellowy green and lists it among the greens in his colour tables [1]. The swatch here leans the other way: the swatch itself looks bluer, and ISCC-NBS block 135 calls it "vivid green" [2]. Books and standards disagree about its hue, and the dictionary's one-line gloss is the outlier [1][2].

The library traces the term to Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, plate 18, which gives 1915 as its first recorded use, and the xkcd color survey of 2010 added it again [2]. It sits between [[sea-green]] and [[seaweed-green]], with [[blue-green]] and [[green]] as its wider relatives [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Ocean green is rare in paint. Only 21 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive carry it, as photographed, which is rarer than 70 per cent of the named colors [3]. Five of them date from the 1800s [3]. The earliest dated match is a Metropolitan Museum painting of 1644, and the archive's early centuries are thin, so that is a floor, not a first [3].

openers: Paterson's dictionary calls ocean green yellowy; the standard swatch is a bluish sea-green.
